decisive_items: a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion measuring 16.1 × 7.9 × 8.1 cm in the abdominopelvic region
a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
Although tumor markers were normal, the imaging findings were concerning for an ovarian neoplasm.
response.rationale: The imaging shows a large solid-cystic adnexal mass with normal tumor markers, most consistent with an ovarian neoplasm. The lifelong lymphedema and double IVC are incidental congenital findings, not explained by other candidates. Meigs syndrome lacks ascites/pleural effusion; fibroids are separate; filarial infection is seronegative; lymphedema is a symptom, not the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Uterine fibroids are present but do not explain the large adnexal mass or lymphedema.
Filarial serology was negative, excluding this infection.
Lymphedema is a clinical finding, not the underlying cause of the adnexal mass.
Meigs syndrome requires ascites and pleural effusion, which are absent; the mass is not specified as fibroma.
